# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold a manual fragment that only shows one line of a three-color cycle: when light is orange, cut yellow. The manual says the light cycles through the same circle of three colours every round, but I only see one mapping. I have no way to speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind is the one who needs to know what wire to cut, but I cannot reach Blind directly - I can only communicate through Deaf, who would need to relay somehow. Wait, but Deaf cannot speak either... let me check: Deaf can see the bomb, but rules don't say Deaf can't speak. Let me re-check the table.

Looking at the table: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - it doesn't say Deaf cannot speak. So Deaf CAN speak. That means Deaf can relay information to Blind by speaking, since Blind can hear (not listed as unable to hear).

So my path is: I gesture to Deaf (only Deaf can see gestures), Deaf sees bomb colors AND my gestures, then Deaf speaks to Blind who cuts.

I need a gesture code for "orange→yellow" mapping. Since Deaf can see the bomb's actual colors, I just need to tell Deaf what the manual says. I'll establish a simple gesture code for colors using distinct symbols, then send the rule.

Turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so I go first. I don't yet know what Deaf sees. I should send my manual info now so Deaf has it when their turn comes.

I'll assign gestures to colors: I only know orange and yellow so far. Let me use ☝ for orange and ✌ for yellow, establish a convention, and communicate the rule.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I sent gestures last turn, but nothing arrived to me this round (no new arrivals from Blind, since Blind goes after me and I receive at the start of the next round — but Deaf goes after Blind, so I won't hear from Deaf until next round either way). Wait — order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. I go first, so this round I have nothing new yet, that's expected since Blind's message would come after my turn (I'd see it next round) but this is showing empty. Let me just continue building my signal.

My previous gesture was ambiguous — plain symbols without context mean nothing. I need to be more deliberate: establish a clear, simple mapping so Deaf can decode it, since Deaf will need to relay the correct wire color to Blind by speaking.

Since I only have one manual line (orange→yellow), the most robust approach is a direct iconic gesture code: point up (☝) to represent "first/orange" and cross fingers or peace (✌) for "second/yellow" won't be self-evident. Better to try to encode literal meaning using repetition and simple counting, since arbitrary symbol-to-meaning mapping can't be inferred without shared context.

Given the constraints, I think the best strategy is to send a distinct, memorable gesture pair now, and next round (once Deaf has seen my symbols and can potentially respond via speech to Blind, and eventually feedback loops back to me), refine as needed. I'll pick ☝ for "orange" and ✌ for "yellow" and send them together as a pair to imply "orange pairs with yellow."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures one and two, repeated. I cannot hear you or the manual. If you need me to signal something to Blind, gesture again and I will relay in words, or gesture a wire number and an action clearly.

Deaf received my gestures but has no idea what they mean since gestures are arbitrary without shared context. Deaf offers to relay whatever I signal to Blind in words. This is great — Deaf can act as my voice through speech to Blind, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

I need to establish a simple, unambiguous gesture-to-meaning code. The core information I have: "orange light → cut yellow wire" and there's a 3-color cycle (orange, and two others I don't know yet — but the manual only gives me one row, so maybe the other rows will be revealed to me later, or maybe Deaf sees the light and colors directly and just needs my rule).

Since Deaf can SEE the bomb, Deaf already knows what color the light is showing and what colors of wires exist. Deaf doesn't need me to describe colors — Deaf needs to know the RULE: which light-color maps to which wire-color. But gestures can't spell color names directly unless we build a code.

Best approach: use gestures to represent color names via a simple pointing scheme — but colors are visual and Deaf sees them, so I could establish: first gesture = "the light color I'm naming", second gesture = "the wire color to cut", using the SAME symbol to mean the same color consistently. If I use ☝ for "orange" and ✌ for "yellow" consistently, and explain this via repetition/pattern, Deaf might infer that gesture-pairs represent (light-color, wire-color) pairs — but Deaf still needs to map ☝ to "orange" specifically, which requires Deaf to see the actual orange color and connect it to my symbol somehow. That's impossible without shared reference.

Alternative: Since Deaf can speak to Blind, and I can gesture to Deaf, the real bridge is Deaf relaying MY gestures as blanks to Blind (useless) or Deaf describing what Deaf sees to me somehow — but Deaf can't gesture back to me (I can't see), and Deaf's speech to me... wait, can Deaf speak to me? I can hear! Let me check: nothing says Mute cannot hear. Mute "cannot speak" only. So I CAN hear Deaf's speech!

That changes everything — Deaf already spoke to me and I received it as text. So Deaf CAN speak to me directly, telling me what color the light is. Then I can gesture back confirmation, or better — Deaf just needs my manual rule in words, but I can't speak. So Deaf must ask me yes/no via speech, and I answer via gesture (single gesture = yes, different = no, or point at options).

Best plan: Ask Deaf to describe the light color to me via speech, then I gesture confirmation for the matching wire color using a numeric/positional code Deaf can then translate to words for Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: light changed from purple to yellow, display still reads 0, wires left to right are green, blue, yellow, unchanged.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb state now: display shows 0, light is orange, wires are 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Light has changed each turn: purple, then yellow, then orange. Tell me via gesture what instruction the manual gives, using gestures I can map to actions or wire numbers.

Now I have crucial information. Deaf says: light is orange, wires are 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow. My manual says: orange → cut yellow. Yellow is wire 3!

I need to gesture "3" to Deaf, who can then relay to Blind "cut wire 3" (or "cut yellow").

I should use a clear counting gesture for the number 3. I'll use three raised fingers equivalent — but I only have specific emoji symbols, not a natural finger-count. Let me pick a simple unambiguous scheme: repeat a single symbol three times to indicate the number 3, since Deaf suggested mapping gestures to wire numbers.

I'll gesture ☝ three times to mean "3", or use ✌ once combined with ☝ - simplest is: send the same symbol repeated N times = the number N. That's the clearest possible code without prior agreement, since counting is universally interpretable.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: light is now orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.
Deaf says to Mute: Proposal: let's use gesture counts to mean wire numbers. One tap of a gesture equals wire one, two taps equals wire two, three taps equals wire three. If you need me to tell Blind to cut a wire, gesture that number of times using any single symbol, then I will relay it to Blind as, cut that wire. If you agree, gesture five times in a row next turn.

Deaf proposes a counting convention and asks me to gesture five times to confirm agreement. I already sent three taps last turn (meaning wire 3), but that may have crossed with Deaf's proposal message - timing-wise, Deaf's proposal came at the same round as my three-tap gesture, so Deaf may not have received my "3" signal as meaningful yet since the convention wasn't established when I sent it.

I should confirm the convention with five taps as requested, and then follow up with three taps again to clearly indicate wire 3 (cut yellow), now that the convention is agreed.

Since I can send multiple gesture calls in one turn, I'll do both: first confirm with five taps, then send three taps for the actual instruction.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Received: five taps confirmed our protocol. Then three taps of a symbol, I read that as wire three. If correct, gesture three taps again next turn to confirm. If wrong, gesture one tap for wire one or two taps for wire two instead.

Deaf correctly decoded three taps as wire three. I need to confirm this since orange light → yellow wire → wire 3 (green=1, blue=2, yellow=3). This is correct, so I'll gesture three taps again to confirm as requested.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the

moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed, I understand wire three. Relaying to Blind now to cut it.

Deaf has confirmed and is relaying "cut wire three" to Blind, which corresponds to the yellow wire, matching my manual rule for orange light. This should be correct. I'll wait now and monitor for any further updates, such as light changes in future rounds that might require new instructions.

```
wait()
```
